# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 4
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
19 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** Elihoreph and-Ahijah, sons-of Shisha — scribes; Jehoshaphat son-of Ahilud — the-recorder;

**LOGOS (formal):** Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, were scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha — royal secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud — court historian;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-Azariah son-of Nathan — over the-governors; and-Zabud son-of Nathan — priest, friend-of the-king;

**LOGOS (formal):** Azariah son of Nathan was over the governors; Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's friend;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Azariah son of Nathan — chief of the district governors; Zabud son of Nathan — priest and personal adviser to the king;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-Ahishar — over the-house; and-Adoniram son-of Abda — over the-forced-labor.

**LOGOS (formal):** Ahishar was over the household; and Adoniram son of Abda was over the forced labor.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Ahishar — palace administrator; Adoniram son of Abda — head of the labor force.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, and-they-provided for the-king and-his-household — each-one a-month in-the-year he-would-provide.

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household. Each one had to make provision for one month in the year.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon had twelve district governors over all Israel. They were responsible for supplying food for the king and his household — each governor for one month of the year.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** Ben-Hesed, in-Arubboth — to-him was Socoh and-all the-land-of Hepher;

**LOGOS (formal):** Ben-Hesed, in Arubboth — to him belonged Socoh and all the land of Hepher;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Ben-Hesed, in Arubboth, including Socoh and the whole region of Hepher;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 11
**EMET (literal):** Ben-Abinadab — all the-height-of Dor; Taphath daughter-of Solomon was his-wife;

**LOGOS (formal):** Ben-Abinadab, in all the height of Dor — he had Taphath the daughter of Solomon as his wife;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Ben-Abinadab, over the entire coastal district of Dor — he was married to Solomon's daughter Taphath;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** Baana son-of Ahilud — Taanach and-Megiddo and-all Beth-shan that is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from-Beth-shan to-Abel-meholah, to beyond Jokmeam;

**LOGOS (formal):** Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth-shan that is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shan to Abel-meholah, as far as the other side of Jokmeam;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Baana son of Ahilud, over Taanach, Megiddo, and all of Beth-shan near Zarethan south of Jezreel, from Beth-shan to Abel-meholah and beyond Jokmeam;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** Ahimaaz — in-Naphtali; he also took Basemath daughter-of Solomon as-wife;

**LOGOS (formal):** Ahimaaz, in Naphtali — he also took Basemath the daughter of Solomon as his wife;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Ahimaaz, in Naphtali — he too married a daughter of Solomon, Basemath;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 20
**EMET (literal):** Judah and-Israel were many, as-the-sand that is by the-sea in-multitude, eating and-drinking and-rejoicing.

**LOGOS (formal):** Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea. They ate and drank and were happy.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as sand on the seashore. They ate, they drank, and they were happy.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 21
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon was ruling over-all the-kingdoms from the-River to-the-land-of the-Philistines and-to the-border-of Egypt. They-were-bringing tribute and-serving Solomon all the-days-of his-life.

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon's kingdom extended from the Euphrates River through Philistine territory all the way to the border of Egypt. The subject nations paid tribute and served Solomon throughout his reign.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 22
**EMET (literal):** And-the-provision-of Solomon for-one day was thirty cors-of fine-flour and-sixty cors-of meal,

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon's provision for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon's daily provisions included thirty cors of fine flour, sixty cors of meal,

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** For he was-ruling over-all the-region across the-River, from-Tiphsah to-Gaza, over-all the-kings across the-River. And-peace was-his on-every side all-around.

**LOGOS (formal):** For he had dominion over all the region west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings west of the Euphrates. And he had peace on all sides around him.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He controlled everything west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza — every king in the region. And he had peace on every border.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** And-Judah and-Israel dwelt in-safety, each-man under his-vine and-under his-fig-tree, from-Dan to-Beer-sheba, all the-days-of Solomon.

**LOGOS (formal):** Judah and Israel lived in safety, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Throughout Solomon's reign, from one end of the land to the other — from Dan to Beersheba — every family in Judah and Israel lived in safety, each under their own vine and fig tree.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** And-these governors provided for the-king Solomon and-for-all who-came-near to the-table-of the-king Solomon, each-one in-his-month; they-let-nothing be-lacking.

**LOGOS (formal):** Those governors provided for King Solomon and for all who came to King Solomon's table, each one in his month. They let nothing be lacking.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The district governors kept King Solomon's table supplied, each during his assigned month. They made sure nothing was lacking.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 28
**EMET (literal):** And-the-barley and-the-straw for-the-horses and-for-the-swift-steeds they-would-bring to the-place where it-would-be, each-one according-to his-charge.

**LOGOS (formal):** Barley and straw for the horses and swift steeds they brought to the place where it was required, each according to his charge.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** They also brought barley and straw to the designated stations for the chariot horses and draft animals, each governor filling his quota.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 29
**EMET (literal):** And-God gave wisdom to-Solomon and-understanding exceedingly much, and-breadth-of heart as-the-sand that is on the-shore-of the-sea.

**LOGOS (formal):** And God gave Solomon wisdom and understanding beyond measure, and breadth of mind like the sand on the seashore.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** God gave Solomon wisdom and insight beyond anything measurable — a mind as vast as sand on the seashore.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 31
**EMET (literal):** And-he-was-wiser than-all men — than-Ethan the-Ezrahite, and-Heman and-Calcol and-Darda, the-sons-of Mahol. And-his-name was in-all the-nations all-around.

**LOGOS (formal):** For he was wiser than all other men — wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. And his fame was in all the surrounding nations.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He was wiser than anyone — wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. His reputation spread to every surrounding nation.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 33
**EMET (literal):** And-he-spoke of the-trees, from the-cedar that is in-Lebanon to the-hyssop that-comes-out in-the-wall. And-he-spoke of the-beasts and-of the-birds and-of the-creeping-things and-of the-fish.

**LOGOS (formal):** He spoke of trees, from the cedar that is in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall. He spoke also of beasts, of birds, of creeping things, and of fish.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He could speak knowledgeably about plant life, from the great cedar of Lebanon to the tiny hyssop growing out of a wall. He studied animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 34
**EMET (literal):** And-they-came from-all the-peoples to-hear ʾet-the-wisdom-of Solomon, from-all the-kings-of the-earth who had-heard ʾet-his-wisdom.

**LOGOS (formal):** And people came from all nations to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** People came from every nation to hear Solomon's wisdom — sent by kings around the world who had heard of his reputation.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
